The election coincided with elections to other federal and state offices. Incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] governor [[Matt Mead]] ran for re-election to a second term in office. Mead won the election with 59% of the vote, defeating [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrat]] Pete Gosar, [[Independent (politician)|Independent]] candidate Don Wills and [[Libertarian Party (United States)|Libertarian]] Dee Cozzens. ==Republican primary== ===Candidates=== ====Declared==== * Taylor Haynes, physician, rancher and Independent write-in candidate for governor [[2010 Wyoming gubernatorial election|in 2010]]{{cite web|url=http://kgab.com/haynes-announces-run-for-governor/|title=Haynes Announces Run For Governor|date=April 29, 2013|access-date=January 20, 2014|work=KGAB.com|author=Doug Randall}} * Cindy Hill, State Superintendent of Public Instruction{{cite web|url=http://kgab.com/hill-announces-run-for-governor-in-2014/|title=Hill Announces Run for Governor in 2014|date=January 31, 2013|access-date=January 20, 2014|work=KGAB.com|author=Doug Randall}} * [[Matt Mead]], incumbent governor{{cite web|url=http://meadforgovernor.com/governor-matt-mead-announces-2014-re-election-campaign|title=Governor Matt Mead Announces 2014 Re-Election Campaign|date=March 11, 2014|access-date=March 12, 2014|work=meadforgovernor.com|author=Kari Gray|archive-date=March 13, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140313044828/http://meadforgovernor.com/governor-matt-mead-announces-2014-re-election-campaign/|url-status=dead}} ===Polling=== {| class="wikitable" |- valign= bottom ! style="width:145px;"| Poll source ! style="width:160px;"| Date(s)
